Question: If there is a 200 in 1,000,000 chance to get bit by a shark, what are the odds that in a group of 4,000 people at least one will get bit in the next year? How about the next three years?
Answer: A2A: We must assume that all 4000 of these people swim in the ocean and that the ‘statistic’ only applies to people who swim in the ocean. The probability that no one is bitten in a year is ( 4999 / 5000 ) 4000 ≈ 0.4493.  So the probability of at least one is about 0.5507.  Cubing the probability of no one for one year (about 0.0907 ), we get about 0.9093.

Question: Sam has 6 sticks, all different lengths, from which he can make an equilateral triangle with two sticks along each side. Five of his 6 sticks measure 25,29,33,37 and 41. How many different lengths are possible for his 6th stick. A.1 B.2 C.3 D.4 E.5?
